Lutsk New Karaite Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volynska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery served the Karaite community of Lutsk, established in 1861. Jews are first mentioned in Lutsk in 1388, with a synagogue and cemetery by the early 16th century; alongside its Rabbinic Jewish community, the town held a historic Karaite presence, with 84 Jewish and 20 Karaite houses recorded at the time of the Khmelnytsky uprising, reduced to 29 and 3 respectively after the community's near-destruction. The distinguished Karaite scholar Avraham Samuel Firkovich is counted among the community's notable figures; 83 Karaites lived in Lutsk by 1886, and 62 remained in 1937. By 1939, the wider Jewish population reached about 19,000 (47 percent); following the June 1941 Nazi arrival, 5,000 Jews were murdered immediately, with the ghetto's final liquidation on September 3, 1942 claiming 25,000 more. In 1979, 700 Jews and 8 Karaites remained in the city.
